record.paper_title: Open problems on countable dense homogeneity
record.context_brief: finite product threshold from CDH to non-CDH
record.original_question: For which natural numbers n does there exist a countable dense homogeneous space X such that every finite power X^i is countable dense homogeneous for i <= n, but X^(n+1) is not countable dense homogeneous?

evidence.quote: Problem 15 (Medini [58]). For which n ∈ ω is there a CDH space X such that Xi is CDH for all i ≤ n while Xn+1 is not CDH?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A topological space $X$ is called countable dense homogeneous (CDH) if for any two countable dense subsets $D_1, D_2 \subseteq X$ there exists a homeomorphism $h: X \to X$ with $h(D_1) = D_2$. For a positive integer $i$, let $X^i$ denote the $i$-fold Cartesian product of $X$ with the product topology.

Determine all natural numbers $n \geq 1$ for which there exists a topological space $X$ such that $X^i$ is countable dense homogeneous for every $i$ with $1 \leq i \leq n$, while $X^{n+1}$ is not countable dense homogeneous.
artifact.status_search_result: The case n=1 has been settled: a zero-dimensional metrizable CDH space X such that X^2 is not CDH has been constructed (using saturated λ-sets, e.g. under Martin's Axiom and in more recent ZFC-ish refinements). Recent work also discusses examples where X^n is CDH but X^(n+1) is not via uncountable saturated λ-sets. However, a complete characterization of all n for which such a space exists does not appear to be established in the literature; the general problem remains open or only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Zero-dimensional metrizable CDH space X such that X^2 is not CDH
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of a zero-dimensional metric CDH space whose square is not CDH, answering questions of Medini.
status_evidence.claim: The case n=1 is resolved: such an X exists.

status_evidence.title: Countable dense homogeneity and λ-sets
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions using saturated λ-sets give CDH spaces with non-CDH higher powers.
status_evidence.claim: Examples of CDH spaces with non-CDH powers exist via λ-set constructions.

status_evidence.title: Countable dense homogeneity in large products of Polish spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of CDH for products; optimality results.
status_evidence.claim: General characterization for all n is not established.
